summary: Guidance on reducing 429 throttling for large batched embedding uploads and recommended rate-limit config
description: Issue summary: Customer is seeing recurring 429 responses when uploading large batched embedding requests (payloads ~800-1200 records per request) during a nightly sync. Impact: Sync jobs are intermittently failing, causing index lag of up to 6 hours. Environment: Dedicated account on prod-us-east running a single reserved pool. Observed behavior: API returns 429 with x-rate-limit-retry-after headers in some batches; other batches succeed. Expected behavior: Large batched uploads should be accepted or throttled predictably with guidance on safe concurrency/throughput settings. Customer asked for prescriptive rate-limit configuration and any platform-side adjustments we recommend.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Prepare a CSV of 1,000 documents and send as 10 concurrent POST /v1/embeddings/batch requests with 100 items each.
2) Run five such job instances in parallel from a single IP to simulate the nightly sync concurrency.
3) Observe 429 responses returned for a subset of requests; check x-rate-limit-* headers.
4) Retry with exponential backoff using original client retry logic and note percentage of successful retries within 2 minutes.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10): Customer provided job logs and a sample payload. They say they previously did smaller batches successfully and increased size during growth. Asked for recommended concurrency and retry strategy.

Luis Romero (SRE) (2026-03-11): Reproduced locally against a dedicated test pool with same quota settings. Observed token- and request-based rate limiter hit when multiple job instances coordinate bursts. Hypothesis: global per-customer request quota is being exceeded transiently due to synchronized job starts.
Luis Romero (2026-03-11): Added link to internal runbook on rate-limit headers: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Rate+Limit+Headers

Support Engineer (2026-03-12): Sent customer a draft of recommended client-side throttling and server-side configuration options. Waiting on customer to confirm if they can spread jobs or accept a minor increase to their reserved capacity window.
Customer (StreamlineSearch) (2026-03-12): Asked whether we can increase request quota for maintenance windows or provide a preferred backoff configuration for batches of 1k+ documents.
investigation_notes: Checked quota-service metrics for customer account: observed short spikes in requests/sec that align with nightly job start times.
Rate limiter behavior: combined enforcement of per-second request ceiling and per-minute token budget. Large batch requests consume both request units and token-equivalent units at higher rates.
Dedicated pool shows sufficient GPU capacity; this is not a serving-runtime saturation issue but a front-door throttling/quotas interaction.
Reproduced 429s by launching 5 parallel job instances with synchronized starts. Spreading start times or limiting concurrency reduced 429s.
Added temporary increase of retry window in client's SDK to 60s with jitter; observed retries succeed in 90% of cases within 45s in test environment.

Potential product-side mitigations evaluated: allow scheduled quota increases (maintenance windows), provide batch size recommendations per model, and surface safer default retry/backoff config in SDK.
resolution: Workaround provided: stagger job start times by 30s increments, limit concurrent job instances to 2 for heavy batches, and implement exponential backoff with full jitter starting at 250ms up to 20s for failed requests.
Temporary customer-side change: reduced batch size to 200 items per request for the nightly sync and observed zero 429s in next run.
Platform guidance: created a support doc draft with prescriptive knobs: per-customer request concurrency, batch-size vs model-cost chart, and suggested SDK retry config. Link shared with customer.

Follow-up actions: Product to evaluate an API option for "maintenance boost" (ticket INT-1462 created) and Docs/SDK team to add a new example for large-batch embedding patterns. Support to re-open if the customer wants a scheduled quota bump.
